per_view.notes: RENDER-A and RENDER-B appear pixel-identical from this camera: same geometry, seams, livery, gear and the same floating speck above the crown. Every criterion ties. Both share the same deviations from the reference: nacelles set aft rather than forward of the wing, hump starting behind the cockpit, and a blunt tail cone.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B are visually indistinguishable at this camera — same geometry, colors, pixel positions. Both share the same flaws: blunt aft fuselage cylinder, nacelles set aft rather than forward of the leading edge, bunched main gear.
RENDER-A and RENDER-B appear pixel-for-pixel identical at this head-on view: same geometry, same livery, same gear and engine placement. No criterion separates them.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B are visually indistinguishable from this rear view — same geometry, colors, gear cluster and fin. Both share the same deviations from the photos: unswept slab fin, no tailplane dihedral, main gear bunched under the belly, all-grey fuselage.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B are pixel-indistinguishable from this planform camera: same geometry, same nacelle placement, same livery, same seams. Both under-scale the nacelle forward offset seen in the reference three-view.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B are pixel-indistinguishable at this camera; every criterion ties. Both share the same weakness versus the photos: the upper-deck hump is far too shallow and short, so the 747 identity is muted.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B are pixel-indistinguishable from this camera: same geometry, livery, gear pose and rear-fuselage seam. Both show a shorter, blockier hump than the photos and a rear-fuselage step the real 747 lacks.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B appear pixel-identical from this camera: same pose, geometry, livery and gear. Both read as 747s but with flat slab pylons, blocky gear, and darker-than-real grey fuselage versus the white photos.
RENDER-A and RENDER-B are visually indistinguishable at this view: same geometry, livery, gear, seams and camera. Both show a partial hump, four pylon-mounted nacelles, and faint fuselage seam rings.

critic.fix_suggestion: Improve 'Four engines under swept wings' (mean 5/10). Target the 8 anchor: four nacelles hung under the swept wings on visible pylons, plausible inboard/outboard spacing; then the 10 anchor: four underslung pylon-mounted nacelles with correct relative size, spacing, and forward offset ahead of the wing leading edge, inlet visibly open/darker.
